text: PR Genius 是面向开源贡献者与维护者的 DSH 网页插件，用于整理已提交的 GitHub PR 并提供下一步建议。它通过侧边栏仪表板、会话标签、右侧面板、设置区和命令接入 DSH，并把分析请求转给 Python FastMCP 引擎。界面可查看知识库、自检信息和进行中的 PR，也提供贡献者与维护者视图。适合希望在 DSH 中跟踪 PR 状态、了解待办事项的用户。宿主侧需配置 Python 分析服务，默认使用 stdio 启动。

PR Genius adds a DSH dashboard and PR guidance surfaces for open source contributors and maintainers. It shows knowledge base status and in flight PRs, routing analysis to a Python FastMCP engine. The host needs that service, launched over stdio by default.
想在 DSH 里集中查看自己发出的开源 PR 进度。

需要一个同时展示 PR 状态和知识库信息的贡献者看板。
Help me track my outstanding open source pull requests and decide what to do next.
I want contribution readiness guidance and PR status in my DSH workspace.
PR Genius 的功能「PR 状态看板」：在 DSH 仪表板展示知识库规模、安装状态和进行中的 PR 摘要，数据由服务层提供。
PR Genius 的功能「贡献建议入口」：通过会话命令调用 Python 引擎的 coach_pr，为 PR 标题、描述和目标仓库请求建议。
PR Genius 的功能「贡献者与维护者视图」：插件配置可启用维护者模式，并设置动作白名单、置信度门槛、陈旧天数和风险档位。

pr-genius README · PR Genius：> Somewhere in your GitHub there are PRs you have stopped opening.
>
> One needs a rebase you keep meaning to do. One has been red for four days and
> nobody told you. Three have sat untouched for three weeks. And one you avoid
> entirely, because opening it would mean confirming that it is dead.

**PR Genius is the board for that work** — the contributions you sent out into
other people's repositories, where you have no tracker, no standup, and no
clue.

pr-genius README · PR Genius：It is **not** a code reviewer. By default it never reads your diff, and it will
never tell you your code is correct. There are good tools for that, and this is
not one of them.

**Unlike PR-Agent or CodeRabbit, this tool does not read your diff.** It does
not write review comments on your code, and it is not an LLM. It scores a PR
against **61 anti-patterns** harvested from PRs that actually got rejected, and
answers a different question from the one a review bot answers.

pr-genius README · PR Genius：It answers the question a working contributor actually has on a Tuesday
morning: **of everything I have sent out, what do I touch today — and what
exactly do I do about it?**

pr-genius README · Why this exists：GitHub remembers the PR.

It does **not** remember why you closed your third attempt on a given repo.
What worked. What didn't. Which reviewer actually answers and which commented
once and vanished. Whether the thing that got you bounced last time was the
size, the missing issue link, or the tone.

That knowledge lives in your head. It dies when the session ends.

PR Genius is where it goes instead.

pr-genius README · Why this exists：> A Repo Profile captures the **what** a project wants.
> A case study captures the **how** a contribution landed or died.
> Your own status history captures the **then-what** — how long it waited, what
> changed, whether it ever came back.

Neither a code reviewer nor a chat model can have the third one. They see your
PR once, in someone else's repo. This sees your portfolio over months.

---

pr-genius README · What it knows：| It knows | Why it matters to you |
|---|---|
| **How 67 large projects actually behave** — merge rates, review cadence, what gets closed | You stop guessing what `encode/httpx` wants and start matching it |
| **Why real PRs got rejected** — written down, with the evidence | You stop repeating the mistake that already cost someone else three weeks |
| **What your own PRs did over time** — which state each sat in, for how long | You find out a PR died *while it was dying*, not three weeks later |
| **The policy of the repo you are aiming at** | A `Fixes #N` in the body is still the single most common reason a first PR gets bounced |

pr-genius README · What it knows：Numbers, for the sceptical: 753 loaded patterns, 190 harvested failed-PR
observations, 68 repo profiles, 302 reviewed cases. Those are receipts for the
sentence above, not the point of it — every one of them is verified against the
live tree on each release by `scripts/verify_claims.py`.

pr-genius README · What it knows：One of those corpora deserves a caveat: `success-patterns/` is
**retrieval/reference only** and is **not wired into scoring**. It is browsable
context, not a positive-feedback system, and no verdict has ever been changed
by it. The 61 anti-patterns are what actually move the risk tier.

---

pr-genius README · The nine states are nine decisions：A number on a dashboard tells you something is wrong. A *state* tells you what
to do about it.
section: The nine states are nine decisions

text:
pr-genius README · The nine states are nine decisions：| State | What it means for you today |
|---|---|
| `NEEDS_REBASE` | Twenty minutes of work and this PR is still alive. |
| `CI_FAILING` | It has been red for days and nobody was going to tell you. |
| `STALE_REVIEW` | Someone looked and stopped. Move now or it goes cold. |
| `STALE_NO_REVIEW` | Nobody looked. Wait, ping, or walk away — but decide. |
| `CLEAN` | Leave it alone. That is also a decision worth being told. |
| `WAITING` | Still inside a normal response window. Go do something else. |

pr-genius README · The two moments it shows up for：**Before you open something.** Is this ready, or am I about to waste a
maintainer's attention?

```bash
python3 -m prgenius coach "fix: timeout in connection pool" \
  --repo encode/httpx --body "Fixes #4821"
```

Five answers, each with a next move — `READY_TO_SUBMIT`, `FIX_BEFORE_SUBMIT`,
`NEEDS_DISCUSSION`, `IMPROVE_CHANCE`, `ASK_MAINTAINER`. It is read-only and
advisory: it never comments, labels, closes or merges anything.

**After it is out there.** Which of these needs me?

pr-genius README · Install：> **What the wheel actually ships.** Since #116, `prgenius-core` bundles the
> decision-relevant corpus — `anti-patterns/`, `profiles/`, `pr-observations/`,
> `docs/policies/`, `locale/` — as `prgenius/data/`, and root resolution finds it
> without a checkout. A clone and `PRGENIUS_REPO_ROOT` are **overrides**, not
> prerequisites.
>
> `success-patterns/` (~2.7 MB) is deliberately **not** bundled: the scorer never
> consults it (#69), so it would triple the wheel without changing a decision.
> `doctor` reports `success_patterns_installed: false` rather than pretending.
>
> ```bash
> prgenius-core doctor      # where the knowledge came from, what it found, what it did not
> ```
>
> `doctor` is the first thing worth running. It reports `repo_root_source` and the
> per-corpus counts on its first lines, and it never lies about what is missing.

pr-genius README · Install：```bash
python3 -m prgenius analyze "feat: add feature" --repo org/repo --body "Fixes #123"
python3 -m prgenius status --author your-handle
python3 -m prgenius profile get owner/name     # what does this project actually want?
```

pr-genius README · What it will never do：- **It will not tell you your code is correct.** It does not judge your logic.
  You can hand it a diff (`--diff`) and it will flag install commands, downloads
  piped into a shell, and secret-shaped strings — a keyword pass, not a review.
  Without one, it looks at the summary counts only.
- **It will not write or send anything on your behalf** unless you pass an
  explicit `--confirm`. Every mutating command is dry-run by default.
- **It will not phone home.** Analysis is local: no LLM, no API key, no network
  call. The commands that touch GitHub do it with *your* token and only for PR
  metadata. There is no telemetry — see [docs/ADOPTION_DATA.md](docs/ADOPTION_DATA.md)
  for what is measured instead and why we chose not to build the rest.
- **It will not pretend.** If a fact is not verified, the docs say so. This
  page has been wrong before and the corrections are in the
  [changelog](CHANGELOG.md).

pr-genius README · What this tool is NOT：The section above is about behaviour. This one is about **roles** — the jobs
people assume it does because of what it looks like. It does not do them, and
that is a boundary, not an oversight.

pr-genius README · What this tool is NOT：| It is not | What that means in practice |
|---|---|
| **A merge gate** | It never blocks a merge and never fails a job. The GitHub Action offers `comment_mode` and `apply_labels` only — there is no required-check integration, because a "gate" that can be ignored is worse than no gate. If you want it to block, wire the Action's exit into *your* branch protection yourself. |
| **A PR title linter** | It will not fail a PR for a malformed title. It will tell you that a missing `Fixes #N` is the most common reason a first PR gets bounced, and leave the decision to you. |
| **A CODEOWNERS-aware reviewer** | It does not know who owns which file, and will not route or request reviewers. |
| **A code reviewer** | See above. It never reads your diff unless you hand one to `--diff`, and what it does then is a keyword pass. |
| **A positive-feedback system** | `success-patterns/` (692 of the 753 loaded patterns) is **retrieval/reference only** and is **not wired into scoring**. Only the 61 anti-patterns can move a verdict. |

pr-genius README · What this tool is NOT：The last row is the one worth internalising: the corpus is large, but the part
that *scores* is small on purpose — it is the part backed by PRs that actually
got rejected.

pr-genius README · 🤖 GitHub Action：Advisory analysis on incoming PRs to a repository you maintain. It never
blocks a merge and never fails a job — every path degrades to a warning.

```yaml
name: PR Genius
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened]

`comment_mode` controls *whether* the analysis is posted as a PR comment:
`never` (default), `high_risk`, or `always` (existing comments are updated in
place — no spam). `comment_on_high_risk: true` still works as an alias.

pr-genius README · 🤖 GitHub Action：`comment_format` controls *how long* that comment is:

- `compact` — **default.** A short bullet list: risk tier, finding counts, the
  one-line summary, and a link to the action run. Around 6 lines.
- `verbose` — the full table: every signal, the whole anti-patterns table, the
  full checklist. Can exceed 100 lines.

pr-genius README · 🤖 GitHub Action：Any other value falls back to `compact` and warns on the run — a typo is never
a reason to post a 100-line comment. The long form is not gone: it lives on the
run page and in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, which is exactly where the compact
comment points.

> **Behavior change worth knowing:** the default is now `compact`, so workflows
> that set `comment_mode` but not `comment_format` post shorter comments than
> they used to. Set `comment_format: verbose` for the old output.

pr-genius README · Version pins：Use a pinned tag (`@v2.1.4`) for reproducibility. There is **no** floating
`v2` tag; the only floating major is `v1`, frozen at `v1.8.0`.

pr-genius README · Docker image：`ghcr.io/zsxh1990/pr-genius` is available if you prefer not to run the
composite action; see the [docs index](docs/index.md) for the `docker://` form.

---

pr-genius README · 🤖 MCP Configuration：`diff_stat` is a summary string (`git diff --stat` output). Size and impact come
from those counts, or from title keywords when no `diff_stat` is given.

pr-genius README · 🤖 MCP Configuration：`diff` (optional) is the unified diff body. When you pass one, a keyword pass over
its **added** lines reports three families: install commands (the typosquat
surface, with the package names), downloads piped into an interpreter, and
secret-shaped strings (reported truncated, never echoed). It is string matching —
it cannot tell you whether a package exists on PyPI and it makes no network call.
The verdict carries `diff_scan.diff_scanned`, so 'looked and found nothing' never
reads as 'did not look'. Pass no diff and nothing about the current behaviour
changes.

pr-genius README · 🧩 DSH Plugin：> **Read this before installing.** The five surfaces are registered by **runtime
> probing**, not by a known-good map. The reason is **not** that the catalog is
> unobtainable — an earlier note here said so, citing `gh api
> repos/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness-sdk` 404, but that is a typo'd repo name; the
> real one, `deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness`, is public and the catalog file
> fetches fine (289,726 bytes at `master`). The reason is that **you do not know
> which SDK version the host has installed**, and the right-hand pane moved
> between them:
>
> | SDK | CLIENT_SLOT_API | `details` | `sidebar.right.pane.tab` |
> |---|---|---|---|
> | `0.0.1-rc.x` | 42 keys | yes | no |
> | `0.2.1-rc.3` | 103 keys | **removed** | **added** (with `.title`) |
>
> Counts are the bracket-matched `CLIENT_SLOT_API` element count, matching
> `npm run smoke:release`'s `catalog keys=` report. So `apply()` tries each
> candidate slot and registers into whichever the host accepts — and if the host
> accepts none of them, **the install looks empty and there is nothing obviously
> wrong**. That is exactly how "empty shell install" shipped eight times in five
> weeks (#86, #90

pr-genius README · PR Genius：> 你的 GitHub 里，有一些 PR 你已经不再点开了。
>
> 有一个需要 rebase，你一直说等会儿弄。有一个红了四天，没人告诉你。
> 有三个摆了三周没人看。还有一个你干脆绕着走——因为点开它，就意味着确认它死了。

**PR Genius 是这些活儿的看板。** 你往别人的仓库发出去的贡献——没有看板、没有站会、没人在替你记着。

它**不是**代码审查工具。它从不读你的 diff，也不会告诉你「代码没问题」。那是另一类工具的活儿，而且有做得很好的。

它回答的是一个真的在干活的人，周二早上会问的问题：**我发出去的这些东西，今天该动哪个——具体怎么做？**

pr-genius README · 为什么会有这个东西：GitHub 记得住那条 PR。

它记不住你为什么关掉了在某个仓库的第三次尝试。什么有效、什么无效。哪个 reviewer 真的会回，哪个评论过一次就消失了。上次把你弹回来的到底是体量、缺 issue 链接，还是语气。

那些东西在你脑子里。会话一结束就没了。

PR Genius 是它们该去的地方。

> 仓库画像记下这个项目**要什么**。
> 案例记下一次贡献**怎么落地或怎么死的**。
> 你自己的状态历史记下**后来怎样**——等了多久、什么变了、有没有回来。

第三样，代码审查工具和大模型都不可能有。它们只在别人的仓库里看见你的 PR 一次。这个看见的是你几个月的组合。

---

pr-genius README · 它知道什么：| 它知道 | 对你意味着 |
|---|---|
| **67 个大项目的实际做派** —— merge 率、review 节奏、什么会被关 | 你不用再猜 `encode/httpx` 想要什么 |
| **真实 PR 为什么被拒** —— 写下来了，带证据 | 你不用再重蹈别人已经赔进去三周的覆辙 |
| **你自己的 PR 后来怎样** —— 每个状态停了多久 | 你在它**正在死的时候**就知道，而不是三周后 |
| **你瞄准的那个仓库的政策** | 正文里一个 `Fixes #N`，仍然是第一条 PR 被弹回来的头号原因 |

给怀疑者看的数字：753 条模式、190 条失败 PR 观察、68 个仓库画像、302 个审过的案例。这些是上面那几句话的**收据**，不是重点——每次发布都会由 `scripts/verify_claims.py` 对着真实目录核一遍。

pr-genius README · 它知道什么：其中一个语料要说清楚：`success-patterns/` **只作检索/参考，不参与评分**。它是可以翻的背景，不是正反馈系统，从来没有改变过任何一次结论。真正推动风险档位的是那 61 条 anti-patterns。

---

pr-genius README · 九个状态，是九个决定：看板上的数字告诉你「有事」。**状态**告诉你「怎么办」。

| 状态 | 今天对你意味着 |
|---|---|
| `NEEDS_REBASE` | 花二十分钟，这条 PR 就还活着。 |
| `CI_FAILING` | 红了好几天，本来不会有人告诉你。 |
| `STALE_REVIEW` | 有人看过，然后停住了。现在动，或者它就凉了。 |
| `STALE_NO_REVIEW` | 没人看过。等、催、还是体面地撤——但要**决定**。 |
| `CLEAN` | 别管它。这同样是一句值得被告知的话。 |
| `WAITING` | 还在正常响应窗口内。去做别的。 |

看板一半的价值，在于告诉你**今天不该把时间花在什么上**。

pr-genius README · 它出现的两个时刻：**在你提之前。** 这个 ready 了吗，还是我准备浪费维护者的注意力？

```bash
python3 -m prgenius coach "fix: timeout in connection pool" \
  --repo encode/httpx --body "Fixes #4821"
```

五个答案，每个都带下一步——`READY_TO_SUBMIT`、`FIX_BEFORE_SUBMIT`、`NEEDS_DISCUSSION`、`IMPROVE_CHANCE`、`ASK_MAINTAINER`。只读、只建议：不评论、不打标签、不关闭、不合并。

**在它已经出去之后。** 这些里面哪个需要我？

```bash
python3 -m prgenius status --author your-handle
```

九个状态、陈旧检测、每条给一个建议——修 CI、rebase、催、等、或者放弃。挂到 cron 上，它就变成你真的会看的那一行。

pr-genius README · 它永远不会做的事：明说，因为这一页的其余部分如果这些含糊，就一文不值：

- **它不会告诉你代码是对的。** 它不读 diff。
- **它不会替你发任何东西**，除非你显式加 `--confirm`。所有会改动状态的命令默认 dry-run。
- **它不外联。** 分析是本地的：无 LLM、无 API key、无网络调用。碰 GitHub 的那几个命令用的是**你自己的** token，而且只读 PR 元数据。没有遥测——见 [docs/ADOPTION_DATA.md](docs/ADOPTION_DATA.md)。
- **它不装。** 没验证过的事实就写没验证。这一页错过，更正在 [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) 里。
